questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The good reputation of the University of Zurich and its affiliated hospitals, as well as Switzerland’s nature and cultural environment.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: An excellent experience, with an amazing study environment, the opportunity to live in a great city like Zurich, and unforgettable experiences exploring Switzerland’s nature.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The welcoming program and initial information meetings were well organized, and the international office was quick and helpful in responding to emails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received assistance through general and medical-specific information meetings, as well as many free activities and offers that helped exchange students get to know each other and experience Zurich and Switzerland.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Very well organized.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not easy to find off-campus housing, as I did not receive an offer from the university and had to search on my own. I was very lucky to find a room in a shared apartment (WG) with two Swiss students, which turned out to be an amazing experience. I strongly recommend starting the housing search early. I found my room through the websites WGZimmer and Flatfox.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus can be challenging to arrange, so it is important to start searching early. Shared apartments are common and a great way to integrate, practice the language, and get to know Swiss culture.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found accommodation on my own, as the housing opportunities provided by the university were fully assigned.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy and helpfull staff.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was well organized and straightforward, with clear instructions provided in advance and support available from the international office when needed.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Support was available from the international office, including guidance on registration, course selection, and any questions via email or in-person meetings.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful – I was able to register for all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Follow the instructions carefully and register as early as possible. Make sure to have a list of your preferred courses ready, as this makes the process smooth and ensures you get the classes you want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very satisfied with the academic program. The experience at both the university and the hospitals was highly educational, engaging, and exciting.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were challenging and stimulating, with a high academic level. They provided both theoretical knowledge and practical skills, especially through hands-on experience at the hospitals.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was more practical compared to UCPH, which I found very beneficial and engaging.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Neurology, Endocrinology, Gynecology and Obstetrics, ENT (Otorhinolaryngology), Ophthalmology, Psychiatry, Radiology, and Internal Medicine.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all courses, but especially Radiology, as it was particularly engaging, well-structured, and provided excellent practical insights.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Registration fees in Switzerland

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transport, food, and housing were more expensive than I expected, as was the general cost of living in Switzerland.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very satisfied. The free sports club ASVZ, with multiple sports centers, was excellent. I tried many different sports, and it was a fun and easy way to socialize.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university offered a variety of activities, including the sports club ASVZ, hiking trips, and cultural walks in Zurich, providing great opportunities for socializing and exploring the city.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: ASVZ sports club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend hiking, skiing, and exploring Switzerland’s beautiful nature. Weekends and holidays are perfect for enjoying the mountains, lakes, and scenic landscapes.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy to adjust. The Swiss culture is welcoming, and interacting with locals and other exchange students helped me settle in quickly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join student clubs and sports activities, attend social events organized by the university, and be open to living in shared apartments (WGs) with local students. These are great ways to meet people and make friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn’t find any cultural differences particularly challenging. The Swiss are friendly and respectful, and I quickly adapted to local customs and routines.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I most appreciated the Swiss respect for punctuality, organization, and cleanliness, as well as their appreciation for nature and outdoor activities.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Start looking for housing early, as university accommodations are limited. Explore Switzerland’s nature and cultural activities. Weekends are perfect for hiking, skiing, and discovering the country.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be proactive in registering for courses and finding housing, make use of the sports clubs and social events to meet people, and budget for the relatively high cost of living in Switzerland. It’s also helpful to learn a few basic German phrases to navigate daily life.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part was gaining hands-on medical experience at the hospitals while living in Zurich, combined with the opportunity to explore Swiss culture and nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was finding off-campus housing, as university accommodations were fully assigned, requiring me to search independently.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
